Core wrapper-authoring skill retained with the Phi engine, per the content distribution design.
Application-owned shared palette definitions stay with the Phi engine; plugin-private palette assets remain with the plugin.
Core managed runtime specifications and locks stay with Phi; each distributed wrapper retains its own process dependencies.

notes: The initial snapshot was copied byte-for-byte. Its original counts are retained in initialImportCounts; current counts reflect the corrected distribution scope.
Shared runtime and application palette definitions were removed from this repository. Contract/design documents remain reference snapshots maintained in Phi.

Eight differential-expression modules now carry executable local Conda specifications and use public frozen container references. Analysis scripts, parameter contracts and wrapper entrypoints are unchanged.
The Phi source repository was not modified by this content-repository correction.

Eighteen existing Phi connector brand icons were copied byte-for-byte into package-local icon files and those connector versions changed to 1.0.1. See docs/content-icons.md for attribution and byte records.
Five Phi omics MCP connectors point at the HTTPS gateway on phi.omicsagent.cn (Streamable HTTP). initialImportCounts.connectors remains 18.

literature-library is the second bundled plugin (toolPrefix lit). 0.6.0 landed with 21 skills; 0.7.0 restructures it into 2 skills (manage-library, compile-wiki) and 12 tools, with tool names changed and no aliases (see its CHANGELOG.md). Demo trees excluded; research-evidence is not merged. counts.plugins is 2; counts.pluginSkills is 4 (visualization 2 + literature-library 2). initialImportCounts stay at the original snapshot.

single-cell-training 0.1.0 ports the scNotebooks analysis steps that the phi-r environment can actually run. Checking resources/runtime/environments/phi-r/environment.yml in Phi shows Seurat, SeuratObject, SingleCellExperiment, ComplexHeatmap, jsonlite, ggplot2, and patchwork present, while monocle3, liana, SoupX, DropletUtils, semla, ArchR, scDblFinder, pheatmap, clusterProfiler, org.Hs.eg.db, SingleR, celldex, miloR, clustree, presto, and hdf5r are absent. The plugin therefore implements inspect/qc/preprocess/markers/annotate/pseudobulk plus an env_probe tool that reports the gap per scNotebooks module, instead of copying install cells that a read-only environment cannot run. A later revision added sc_notebook, because scNotebooks is teaching material and the script-only port lost that: no notebook package type exists in Phi (PackageType is skill/plugin/wrapper/mcp), so the notebook is generated into the user's project rather than distributed. Raw-read processing stays with the wrapper tree. counts.plugins is 3; counts.pluginSkills is 6 (visualization 2 + literature-library 2 + single-cell-training 2). initialImportCounts stay at the original snapshot.

single-cell (renamed from single-cell-training) maintains two parallel toolkits in one plugin: seurat-workflow (R, plugin:seurat, Seurat 6) and scanpy-workflow (Python 3.13, plugin:scanpy, scanpy 1.13), each with its own three-platform conda lock. Since 0.6.0 each route has one analysis source: assets/fragments is the teaching code, scripts are thin flag-to-config adapters plus a JSON report layer, and references/analysis-playbook.md (per-stage call/read/decide/red-line decision procedures for the agent) plus per-step notes in references/step-notes/ carry the knowledge layer, and references/README.md indexes them by function (agent decision docs vs maintainers/ provenance). The scNotebooks curriculum is folded into seurat-workflow/references (no standalone skill). The SingleCell agent routes by the user's R/Python preference and declares no session environment, because each skill's phi.environment wins over the agent binding and only the chosen route's environment needs building. The former standalone resources/skills/scanpy (K-Dense, BSD-3-Clause) is absorbed into scanpy-workflow and removed; its host-install guidance is dropped in favour of the private environment. NBIS workshop-scRNAseq scanpy labs (CC-BY-4.0 per the repository LICENSE; the site footer's GPL-3 label contradicts it) are reference-only with attribution; the fragment code is original. counts.standaloneSkills is 16; counts.pluginSkills is 6 (visualization 2 + literature-library 2 + single-cell 2). initialImportCounts stay at the original snapshot.

metagenomics is the fourth bundled plugin (toolPrefix mg): profiling-workflow (seven mg_* tools) owns the read-based downstream (reports to matrix to rarefaction/diversity/differential/functional tables/figures, with optional clustered heatmaps, SGB strain-level merges via rank T with sgb_species mapping, and an explicit mg_function to mg_differential functional chain) and mag-workflow (six mg_* tools) owns the assembly/MAG downstream (QUAST stats, CheckM/CheckM2 MIMAG grading, quality filtering, joined MAG table with CoverM reliability masking and genome-size-weighted relative abundance, prokka/prodigal/eggNOG annotation summaries with MIMAG structural evidence and KO/COG matrices, and pure-Python GTDB-tree patristic distances). Both run in plugin:metagenomics (Python 3.13 + pandas/numpy/scipy/matplotlib-base, three-platform locks). Upstream classification, assembly, binning, CheckM, GTDB-Tk, annotation and the whole nf-core/mag pipeline stay on wrappers; the mag starter wrapper is expanded to the curated assembly/binning/quality/taxonomy parameter set in the same change, and dRep/CoverM/eggNOG-mapper are post-mag wrapper steps. Database downloads (GTDB ~80+ GB, Kraken2 tens of GB) require disk checks and user consent per the agent rules. counts.plugins 3 to 4, counts.pluginSkills 6 to 8.

spatial-transcriptomics is the fifth bundled plugin (toolPrefix st): spatial-workflow (ten st_py_* tools) owns the spot/bin-level spatial downstream in one private locked environment plugin:spatial (Python 3.12 + scanpy 1.12 + squidpy 1.8 + spatialdata 0.8, three-platform conda locks). It reads 10x Visium (incl. HD bin/seg) and BGI Stereo-seq (GEM/GEF, square bin and cellbin), then runs QC, normalize/PCA/cluster/UMAP, a tissue-coordinate spatial graph, markers and panel annotation, spatially variable genes (Moran/Geary), neighborhood enrichment/co-occurrence, scipy-NNLS deconvolution (needs an scRNA reference; cell2location/tangram are reported as project-environment gaps), ligand-receptor communication (squidpy ligrec with a curated starter resource), and cross-sample differential spatial patterns. assets/fragments is the single analysis source shared by the thin flag-to-config script adapters and the notebook renderer; references/analysis-playbook.md plus per-step references/step-notes/ carry the agent decision layer, and references/maintainers/ records provenance. The knowledge layer is an original distillation of the OSTA book (https://github.com/lmweber/OSTA/, CC-BY-4.0) and seven Stereo-seq application papers (Liu 2022 Dev Cell; Tan 2024 Zool Res; Wu 2024 Cell Discov; Xu 2024 Nat Genet; Kilfeather 2024 Cell Rep; Lei 2024 Cell Metab; Tsubosaka 2023 Cell Rep), with attribution and no copied upstream notebook text/images/data. counts.plugins 4 to 5, counts.pluginSkills 8 to 9.

metabolomics is the sixth bundled plugin (toolPrefix mb): lcms-workflow (nine mb_* tools) owns the untargeted LC-MS feature-table downstream in one private locked environment plugin:metabolomics (Python 3.13 + pandas/numpy/scipy/matplotlib-base, same stack as metagenomics, three-platform conda locks). mb_inspect recognizes xcms/MZmine/MS-DIAL/MetaboAnalyst exports, metadata, MSP/MGF libraries, pathway mappings, compound mass databases and m/z/ID lists (RT unit inference, QC/blank detection); mb_qc filters features by QC-sample RSD (default 30%) and detection rate (default 0.8) and fails without QC samples; mb_preprocess runs impute (NaN and zero count as missing; none/half_min/min/zero) -> normalize (none/tic/median/pqn/is) -> transform (none/log2/log10) in fixed order; mb_multivariate fits PCA (SVD) and PLS-DA (original numpy NIPALS PLS2) with uv/pareto scaling, VIP, R2Y/Q2 cum (LOO CV, 7-fold above n=50, scaling recomputed inside folds) and seeded label-permutation empirical p; mb_univariate runs Welch/Wilcoxon/Kruskal-Wallis + BH FDR + fold change (logged flag) with a volcano; mb_annotate matches 13C isotopes, pos/neg adduct pairs and H2O/CO2 neutral losses within ppm+RT tolerance (seconds/minutes auto-conversion) and groups pseudospectra by union-find with adduct-pair-derived neutral-mass consensus (MSI level 3 caveat); mb_ms2_match parses MSP (NIST/MoNA/RIKEN dialects) and MGF, gates on precursor ppm and scores sqrt-intensity greedy-fragment cosine (MSI level 2 caveat); mb_pathway does ID hypergeometric enrichment or mummichog-style m/z permutation enrichment against user-supplied mappings/databases (nothing built in); mb_plot draws variance-top clustered heatmaps. Upstream peak picking (msconvert, xcms, MZmine, MS-DIAL) has no wrapper in this repository and is reported as a gap, as are OPLS-DA, QC drift correction, GSimp imputation, CAMERA full pseudospectra, formula assignment, SIRIUS/MetFrag/GNPS, GC-MS retention indices, NMR and targeted MRM. Knowledge layer: analysis-playbook (call/read/decide/red-lines), nine step-notes, references README and maintainers/source-map.md. Primary source: RforMassSpectrometry Metabolomics Book (CC-BY-4.0, ideas and structure only, all prose and code original); the two user-requested Zhihu tutorials returned HTTP 403 and are noted as inaccessible in the source map. counts.plugins 5 to 6, counts.pluginSkills 9 to 10.

single-cell-atac is the seventh bundled plugin (toolPrefix scatac): scatac-workflow (ten scatac_* tools: inspect/qc/preprocess/peaks/markers/annotate/motif/integrate/notebook/env_probe) owns the single-cell ATAC downstream in one private locked environment plugin:scatac (Python 3.12 + snapatac2 2.10 + scanpy 1.12 + ipykernel, pure conda, three-platform explicit locks solved against the tuna mirror and rewritten to official conda.anaconda.org URLs; macs3 3.1.0 ships as a snapatac2 dependency). It starts from 10x Cell Ranger ATAC fragments.tsv.gz (or BAM via make_fragment_file, a saved .h5ad, or a peak/tile matrix), then runs QC (n_fragment/frac_dup/frac_mito/TSSe), scrublet doublet removal, spectral embedding, kNN/Leiden/UMAP, per-cluster MACS3 peak calling with a merged peak set and peak-count matrix, marker_regions (cluster-vs-rest) with opt-in pairwise diff_test, gene-activity annotation (panel scoring / scRNA-reference kNN label transfer / explicit mapping), motif enrichment on marker regions, and multi-sample harmony/scanorama/mnc integration. assets/fragments (16 steps, 48 parameters, 6 presets) is the single analysis source shared by the thin flag-to-config script adapters and the language-neutral notebook renderer (RENDERER_VERSION=3); references/analysis-playbook.md, red-line-cheatsheet.md, 16 per-step step-notes/ and maintainers/implementation-notes.md carry the agent decision and provenance layers. chrom_sizes are bundled offline for hg38/mm10/hg19/mm39 and the ENCODE hg38/mm10 blacklist is inlined base64-gzip in assets/fragments/blacklist.py; gene annotation (GFF3 ~50MB) and genome FASTA (~845MB) are snapatac2 lazy downloads supplied by user input-path or reported as gaps, never downloaded into the read-only environment. The TF layer is motif enrichment (a sequence-level prediction), not chromVAR per-cell deviations; gene activity is an accessibility proxy, not measured RNA. Raw-read alignment/Cell Ranger ATAC stay on nf-core wrappers and bulk ChIP/CUT&Tag belong to the planned sibling chromatin-profiling plugin. chromVAR/ArchR/Signac (R route), episcanpy (numpy 2 incompatible), scvi-tools/magic-impute (pip-only) and a TF-gene GRN are reported as project-environment gaps by scatac_env_probe. Knowledge is an original distillation of the SnapATAC2 documentation (MIT) and sc-best-practices (Apache 2.0); the ENCODE blacklist is doi:10.1038/s41598-019-45839-z; no upstream text/images/data are copied. counts.plugins 6 to 7, counts.pluginSkills 10 to 11.

chromatin-profiling is the eighth bundled plugin (toolPrefix chip): chromatin-workflow (nine chip_* tools: inspect/qc/consensus/count/diff/annotate/visualize/notebook/env_probe) owns the bulk ChIP-seq / CUT&Tag / CUT&RUN downstream in one private locked environment plugin:chip (R 4.5 + DiffBind 3.20 + DESeq2 + edgeR + csaw 1.44 + ChIPseeker 1.46 + GenomicAlignments + Rsamtools + GenomicFeatures + ComplexHeatmap + jsonlite, three-platform explicit locks; csaw is platform-gated off darwin-arm64 because bioconda has no osx-arm64 build). It is PURE DOWNSTREAM: it starts from already-called peaks (BED/narrowPeak/broadPeak), a DiffBind sample sheet, a peak x sample count table, indexed BAMs, a bigWig or a saved .rds, and never aligns reads or calls peaks (ChIP upstream is the nf-core/chipseq wrapper; CUT&Tag SEACR upstream has no wrapper and is a reported gap). The chain is inspect -> QC (FRiP + replicate peak-overlap reproducibility) -> blacklist filtering -> consensus peakset -> read counting + normalization -> PCA/UpSet -> differential binding (DiffBind/DESeq2/edgeR primary for TF/narrow marks and CUT&Tag; csaw window-based for broad marks) -> ChIPseeker annotation / TSS profiles against a user-supplied GTF/GFF3 or TxDb. assets/fragments (19 steps) is the single analysis source shared by the thin flag-to-config Rscript adapters and the language-neutral notebook renderer (RENDERER_VERSION=3, same machinery as the sibling plugins); references/analysis-playbook.md, red-line-cheatsheet.md (12 hard red lines), 19 per-step step-notes/ and maintainers/implementation-notes.md carry the agent decision and provenance layers. Annotation is lean by design: no target-genome TxDb/org.db is bundled, ChIPseeker uses makeTxDbFromGFF on the user GTF/GFF3 or loadDb on a user TxDb .sqlite (hg19 is never a silent default), and gene-symbol org.db mapping is a reported gap. The ENCODE v2 hg38 (636 regions) / mm10 (3435 regions) blacklist is inlined base64-gzip inside assets/fragments/blacklist-filter.R for offline self-containment (doi:10.1038/s41598-019-45839-z). csaw on darwin-arm64, IDR, profileplyr, HOMER/MEME motif discovery and org.db gene symbols are reported as project-environment gaps by chip_env_probe. Knowledge is an original distillation of the DiffBind / csaw / ChIPseeker vignettes (Artistic-2.0) and ENCODE ChIP-seq guidelines (Landt doi:10.1101/gr.136184.111); no upstream text/images/data are copied. Single-cell ATAC belongs to the sibling single-cell-atac plugin. counts.plugins 7 to 8, counts.pluginSkills 11 to 12.

Added nine original protein-design Nextflow wrappers inspired by RosettaCommons/chaperone (MIT): six modules (protein_metrics, design_filter, rfd3, ligandmpnn, boltz2, alphafold3), two subworkflows (design_postprocess, seq_fold_eval with predictor switching between boltz2 and alphafold3), and one end-to-end workflow (protein_binder_design). All Nextflow processes, wrapper adapters, and pure-Python bin/ helper scripts are original (MIT) and bundle no model weights or upstream source code; upstream runtimes remain subject to their respective licenses (RFdiffusion3/Foundry BSD-3-Clause, LigandMPNN MIT, Boltz-2 MIT, AlphaFold 3 code Apache-2.0 with non-commercial model parameters supplied separately by the user via model_dir).

protein-design is the ninth bundled plugin (toolPrefix pd, agent ProteinDesign): three skills (protein-design-workflow playbook/tutorials with no scripts; structure-input-prep with pd_inspect_structure and pd_validate_rfd3_spec; design-evaluation with pd_funnel_report) using pure-Python stdlib scripts in the shared phi:python@1 environment. Heavy GPU generation, inverse folding, and structure prediction stay on the nine local Nextflow wrappers (rfd3, ligandmpnn, boltz2, alphafold3, protein_metrics, design_filter, seq_fold_eval, design_postprocess, protein_binder_design). counts.plugins 8 to 9, counts.pluginSkills 12 to 15.

Added three extended protein-design Nextflow module wrappers (MIT original adapters and pure-Python bin/ helpers, no weights bundled): bindcraft (martinpacesa/BindCraft MIT; optional PyRosetta carries a separate non-commercial license), foldseek (steineggerlab/foldseek GPL-3.0, supporting easy-search novelty scoring and easy-cluster structural dereplication), and esmfold2 (biohub/ESMFold2 MIT, fast MSA-free folding with external model_dir).

Added two additional open-source structure prediction modules (MIT original adapters and pure-Python bin/ helpers, no weights bundled): protenix (bytedance/Protenix Apache-2.0, supporting v1/v2 checkpoints) and chai1 (chaidiscovery/chai-lab Apache-2.0, with pure-Python .npz score reader), and wired both into seq_fold_eval and protein_binder_design under predictor (boltz2 | alphafold3 | protenix | chai1).

Upgraded metagenomics plugin to 0.2.0 (counts.pluginSkills 15 to 16) within the same locked Python 3.13 environment (pandas/numpy/scipy/matplotlib): added mg_mag_traits (AMRFinderPlus/ABRicate/RGI/antiSMASH downstream summaries), PERMDISP and multi-covariate marginal PERMANOVA in mg_diversity, mg_network (Spearman co-occurrence network + hubs), mg_classify (leak-free stratified CV mRMR/Mann-Whitney + L2 logistic regression with OOF AUROC/Youden ROC), and amplicon-workflow (mg_amplicon_unifrac for Weighted/Unweighted UniFrac on nf-core/ampliseq / QIIME 2 ASV tables + rooted trees), plus anti-pitfall red lines inspired by MicroBioAgent (bioRxiv 2026.11.17.767465).

Upgraded metagenomics to 0.3.0 (mg_multivariable CLR+OLS and mg_mag_metabolism KEGG/gapseq/SBML GEM summaries) and spatial-transcriptomics to 0.2.0 (interaction matrix, centrality, Ripley L, UTAG-style spatial niches, and spatial PAGA/DPT trajectory).

Added bulk-rna-seq (0.1.0 -> 0.1.1, toolPrefix rna, 6 tools), proteomics (0.1.0 -> 0.2.0, toolPrefix prot, 7 tools including prot_rollup, moderated DE, PTM/KSEA, ORA/GSEA, and co-abundance networks), and genomics (0.1.0, toolPrefix gen, 6 somatic MAF/CNV downstream tools), each with three-platform explicit conda environment locks. counts.plugins is 12; counts.pluginSkills is 19.

Vendored the shared nf-core module and subworkflow wrapper tree plus 10 nf-core workflow wrappers (ampliseq, atacseq, chipseq, mag, methylseq, quantms 1.2.0, rna-seq, rnafusion, sarek 3.12.0, scrnaseq) and 14 local protein-design wrappers, bringing callable wrapper/wrapper.yaml adapters to 2202.

Added scientificContext semantic matrix/table annotations and contract-1.0.0 .phi-artifact.json sidecars across domain plugins: bulk-rna-seq (0.1.1 -> 0.2.0), chromatin-profiling (0.1.1), single-cell (0.6.1), single-cell-atac (0.1.1), spatial-transcriptomics (0.2.1), metabolomics (0.1.1), metagenomics (0.3.1), proteomics (0.2.1), genomics (0.1.1 -> 0.2.0), and local differential-expression wrappers (deseq2, edger, limma, timeseries).

Upgraded genomics to 0.2.0 (gen_vcf2maf annotated VCF to GDC MAF converter with optional FASTA 3-mer Context extraction) and bulk-rna-seq to 0.2.0 (rna_id_map Ensembl/RefSeq version stripping, GTF/table gene mapping, biotype filtering, and collision-aware aggregation; rna_geo_import NCBI GEO Series Matrix + GPL platform importer).

Added clinical-survival (0.1.0, toolPrefix clin, agent ClinicalSurvival, skill survival-workflow) as the thirteenth bundled plugin (counts.plugins 12 to 13, counts.pluginSkills 19 to 20) in locked Python 3.13 environment plugin:clinical: clin_inspect (cohort event/time polarity, reverse-KM follow-up, EPV budget), clin_table1 (stratified Table 1 with Shapiro-Wilk normality routing, Welch/ANOVA/Mann-Whitney/Kruskal-Wallis, Fisher/chi-square, SMD), clin_km (Kaplan-Meier curves, log-log Greenwood 95% CIs, log-rank test, aligned Number-at-Risk subplot), clin_cox (Breslow univariable/multivariable Cox PH, Harrell C-index, Schoenfeld PH diagnostics, HR forest plot), and clin_time_roc (IPCW time-dependent ROC at clinical landmarks + leak-free stratified K-fold L2-penalized Cox signature).

Added multi-omics (0.1.0 -> 0.1.1, toolPrefix mo, agent MultiOmics, skill multiomics-workflow) and methylation (0.1.0 -> 0.1.1, toolPrefix meth, agent Methylation, skill methylation-workflow) as the fourteenth and fifteenth bundled plugins (counts.plugins 13 to 15, counts.pluginSkills 20 to 22), upgraded single-cell to 0.7.0 -> 0.7.1 (sc_py_communication heteromeric ligand-receptor permutation screening + Preset 8 + output schemas), and updated chromatin-profiling to 0.1.2 -> 0.1.3 (pointing CUT&Tag peak calling to the vendored nf-core/seacr/callpeak module wrapper + output schemas).

Added mendelian-randomization (0.1.0, toolPrefix mr, agent MendelianRandomization, skill mr-workflow: mr_gwas_qc, mr_harmonize, mr_estimate, mr_coloc) and pharmacogenomics (0.1.0, toolPrefix pgx, agent Pharmacogenomics, skill pgx-workflow: pgx_dose_response, pgx_synergy, pgx_biomarker) as the sixteenth and seventeenth bundled plugins (counts.plugins 15 to 17, counts.pluginSkills 22 to 24), upgraded bulk-rna-seq to 0.3.0 (adding rna_coexpression WGCNA-style co-expression modules/hubs and rna_tme_deconv ESTIMATE + NNLS immune deconvolution), enforced 100% script output JSON schemas across literature-library (0.7.1), single-cell (0.7.1), single-cell-atac (0.1.3), spatial-transcriptomics (0.2.2), and chromatin-profiling (0.1.3), removed the broken duplicate nf-core/rna-seq/wrapper/workflows file, and added tests/contracts.test.mjs.

Decoupled specialty visualization and domain packages from Phi's shared base environments (phi:python@1, phi:r@1): upgraded visualization to 1.3.0 with its own locked multi-platform private environment plugin:viz (environments/viz/environment.yml + three-platform explicit locks covering R 4.4, Python 3.12, 45 visualization CRAN/Bioconductor packages, and 8 pinned GitHub sourcePackages), and gave standalone skills rdkit and scvelo self-contained skill-local environments (./environment.yml + three-platform explicit locks) so phi-python and phi-r stay lean general-purpose Notebook/Office/data-science bases.

Curated standalone research skills catalog (counts.standaloneSkills 16 to 22): removed four misplaced single-library manuals (anndata, scvelo, scikit-survival, pysam) whose domains are covered by plugins/wrappers and removed from phi-python, and added ten zero-dependency MIT-licensed research workflow skills (manuscript-writing, manuscript-polishing, humanizer, peer-review-response, manuscript-review, nsfc-proposal, literature-review, paper-reading, statistical-review, paper-to-slides) built on a unified first-principles SKILL.md standard with true on-demand references/ for multi-branch skills.

Replaced the single-skill clinical-survival plugin with the unified clinical plugin (0.1.0, toolPrefix clin, agent Clinical, private environment plugin:clinical, two skills survival-workflow + prediction-causal-workflow covering 11 clin_* tools: inspect, table1, km, cox, time_roc, competing_risk, diagnostic_roc, calibration_dca, psm_iptw, rcs, meta) and added the crispr plugin (0.1.0, toolPrefix crispr, agent Crispr, private environment plugin:crispr, two skills guide-design-workflow + screen-editing-workflow covering 6 crispr_* tools: design_guides, offtarget_scan, library_check, screen_qc, screen_hits, editing_quant, paired with upstream nf-core mageck/crisprcleanr/crispresso2/bowtie wrappers). counts.plugins 17 to 18, counts.pluginSkills 24 to 27.

Consolidated standalone research workflow skills into 10 high-cohesion zero-dependency MIT skills (counts.standaloneSkills 22): study-design (hypotheses + experimental/power design), statistical-review, literature-review (1-3 paper deep reading + >=5 paper synthesis), grant-proposal (NSFC + NIH/NSF/ERC), manuscript-writing, manuscript-polishing, manuscript-review (mock review + citation audit + FAIR data/code availability), peer-review-response, humanizer, and paper-to-slides.

Authored in phi-packages. Ports the executable analysis steps of the scNotebooks single-cell curriculum (https://github.com/integrativebioinformatics/scNotebooks, commit 55229bb496f5b6b96eae266ac867e5068d600464) into a Phi plugin: seven Seurat script tools in skills/seurat-workflow, plus a reference-only curriculum map in skills/scnotebooks-curriculum. No notebook text, image, or data file is copied; the upstream notebooks remain CC BY 4.0 (Rojas-Hidalgo et al., Nat Genet, 2026). 0.2.0 adds a notebook path (tool sc_notebook): it generates a runnable R notebook in the user's project with real inline Seurat code plus explanations, for modules 4, 5, 8, and 9, and can execute every cell once as a self check. No .ipynb is stored in this repository: the skill contract forbids executing anything from assets/, and Phi's notebook tools operate on the user's project, so the notebook is generated there against the already-installed phi-r R kernel. 0.3.0 refactors sc_notebook into a fragment library (assets/fragments) plus a deterministic renderer: the agent passes steps and parameter values, the renderer fills placeholders into one finished notebook with a single config cell, inject/merge sources, relative paths, and render provenance; step selection and threshold decisions stay with the agent per SKILL.md rules. The plugin id is renamed from single-cell-training to single-cell to match its analysis scope, title, agent, and tool prefix. 0.4.0 ships a plugin-private environment (environments/seurat: R 4.5 + Seurat 6.0.0 + IRkernel, with three-platform explicit locks; Seurat 6.0.0, RcppThread 2.4.0 and GenomeInfoDbData pinned as sourcePackages because no usable conda build exists) instead of borrowing phi:r@1, so the script chain and the notebook stay on one pinned version. The notebook kernel becomes plugin-single-cell-seurat, synced by Phi's managed-kernel sync for enabled plugin environments that ship r-irkernel or ipykernel. 0.5.0 adds a parallel Python toolkit in the same plugin: skills/scanpy-workflow (ten sc_py_* tools) with its own private environment (environments/scanpy: Python 3.13 + scanpy 1.13 + ipykernel, three-platform explicit locks; bbknn reported as a gap because bioconda has no py313 build), notebook presets 1-7 adapted from the NBIS workshop-scRNAseq scanpy labs (https://nbisweden.github.io/workshop-scRNAseq/, CC-BY-4.0 per the repository LICENSE — the site footer's GPL-3 label contradicts it; reference-only: fragment code is original and attribution is carried in preset intros and these notes), and a byte-identical shared build_notebook.py renderer across both skills (asserted by a repository test). The SingleCell agent routes by the user's R/Python preference and declares no session environment, because each skill's phi.environment wins over the agent binding. The former standalone resources/skills/scanpy skill (K-Dense, BSD-3-Clause) is absorbed into scanpy-workflow and removed. 0.6.0 unifies each route on one analysis source: assets/fragments is the teaching code executed by both the notebook renderer and the script tools (scripts/_fragments runs the same fragments; tool scripts are thin flag-to-config adapters; scripts/reports only serializes JSON; fragment chatter goes to stderr so stdout stays one JSON). Field-by-field parity against the pre-refactor reports: R 7/7 and Python 10/10 identical modulo output paths. The scnotebooks-curriculum skill is folded into seurat-workflow/references (plugin skills 3 to 2, repo plugin skills 7 to 6, total skills 23 to 22). A knowledge layer is added: 30 per-step notes in references/step-notes/ (purpose/principle/interpretation/pitfalls, the notebook's teaching cells, paired to fragments by step id) and references/analysis-playbook.md in both skills — the agent's decision manual, per stage call/read/decide/red-lines with threshold starting points grounded in the tools' JSON contracts — plus references/README.md indexing by function (agent decision docs, step notes and cross-route handoff vs maintainers/ provenance); skill directories are organized by function (assets holds only render source material: flat assets/fragments code plus assets/steps.json presets; all Markdown lives in references); original prose distilled from OSCA (CC BY 4.0), sc-best-practices (Apache 2.0; Heumos, Schaar, Lance et al., Nat Rev Genet 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41576-023-00586-w), the Cambridge/Hemberg singlecellcourse.org course (GPL-3, not OSCA), and the NBIS labs. The NBIS license is corrected everywhere to CC-BY-4.0 per the repository LICENSE (the site footer's GPL-3 label contradicts it). The renderer gains bool/list parameter types and stays byte-identical across skills; show_plot prints inline only under IRkernel so Rscript runs no longer leave Rplots.pdf in the working directory.

Authored in phi-packages. Metagenomics plugin (toolPrefix mg, agent Metagenomics) with two downstream script-chain skills and one private locked environment (Python 3.13 + pandas/numpy/scipy/matplotlib-base; three-platform explicit locks solved with micromamba against the tuna mirror and rewritten to official conda.anaconda.org URLs). profiling-workflow (seven tools): mg_inspect identifies Kraken2/Bracken/MetaPhlAn/MPA/HUMAnN reports, matrices, samplesheets, QUAST reports, bin quality tables, prokka/prodigal/eggNOG outputs and Newick trees; mg_merge builds one taxa x sample matrix per kind and rank (Kraken2 clade reads and Bracken re-estimated reads are counts, MetaPhlAn is relative abundance 0-100; kinds never mixed; rank T keeps MetaPhlAn/MPA SGB strain-level rows and returns an sgb_species mapping); mg_rarefaction draws seeded observed-richness rarefaction curves on integer-count matrices (sequential hypergeometric subsampling, mean +/- sd bands, optional group coloring, not-plateaued flags; rejects relative abundances and fractional estimates); mg_diversity computes observed/Chao1/Shannon/Simpson/InvSimpson (first two counts-only), Bray-Curtis, PCoA and seeded PERMANOVA; mg_differential runs Mann-Whitney U with tie correction (log2FC + effect r) or Kruskal-Wallis plus BH FDR and a volcano; mg_function normalizes/regroups/splits HUMAnN-style tables (plain column renormalization, not stratification-aware renorm; normalized/regrouped tables feed mg_differential with values=relative, mg_diversity and mg_plot); mg_plot draws composition barplots and heatmaps with optional log10 transform and average-linkage hierarchical clustering of rows/columns. mag-workflow (six tools): mg_assembly_stats parses QUAST report.tsv (>=0 bp rows); mg_bin_qc grades CheckM2/CheckM tables into MIMAG-style tiers with the caveat that strict HQ also needs rRNA/tRNA evidence; mg_bin_filter copies passing bins with a manifest; mg_mag_table left-joins quality + GTDB-Tk summary (rank columns) + CoverM + dRep Cdb clusters, masks CoverM Means below a covered-fraction floor (default 0.3) and optionally adds genome-size-weighted per-sample relative abundances (single- and multi-sample CoverM columns), and plots MAGs per phylum; mg_mag_function summarizes prokka per-bin directories (.txt counts + .tsv 5S/16S/23S rRNA and tRNA>=18 MIMAG structural evidence, prediction-level), prodigal .faa/.gff (.gz) gene counts and eggNOG-mapper .emapper.annotations into bin x KO / bin x COG matrices plus a COG stacked barplot (deterministic bin attribution with --bin_map override); mg_mag_tree parses GTDB-Tk classify.tree Newick in pure Python (no phylogenetics dependency) into a MAG patristic distance matrix and a nearest-reference table (--summary identifies user tips exactly, else a reference-pattern heuristic). Heavy steps stay on wrappers: module wrappers plus the vendored nf-core/mag 5.5.0 workflow, whose starter wrapper is expanded in the same change from 5 to 43 curated parameters (defaults in params.json); dRep and CoverM are documented as post-mag wrappers because mag 5.5.0 does not include them (mag does run prodigal/prokka; eggNOG-mapper is a separate post-mag wrapper). Knowledge layer: two analysis-playbooks (call/read/decide/red-lines), thirteen step-notes, references READMEs and maintainers/source-map.md with citations. Sources: EasyMetagenome v1.24/EasyMicrobiome (GPL-3.0; Liu et al., iMeta 2025, DOI 10.1002/imt2.70001) for stage ordering, QC defaults and dRep conventions; the local Snakemake Workflow Meta rules for tool pairing and file shapes; sib-swiss/metagenomics-data-analysis-training (GPL-3.0, ideas only, no text or code copied); cambiotraining/metagenomics (CC BY 4.0, attribution in both source-maps, no verbatim text); nf-core/mag nextflow_schema.json for parameter names/defaults. All scripts and prose are original; no upstream code, text, images or data are distributed. v0.1.0 is script chains plus knowledge only, no notebook renderer.

Authored in phi-packages. Metabolomics plugin (toolPrefix mb, agent Metabolomics) with one downstream script-chain skill (lcms-workflow, nine mb_* tools: inspect/qc/preprocess/multivariate/univariate/annotate/ms2_match/pathway/plot) and one private locked environment (Python 3.13 + pandas/numpy/scipy/matplotlib-base; three-platform explicit locks solved with micromamba 2.1.1 dry-run against the tuna mirror and rewritten to official conda.anaconda.org URLs; only fontconfig differs from the metagenomics locks due to an upstream rebuild). Untargeted LC-MS feature tables only: vendor export recognition (xcms/MZmine/MS-DIAL/MetaboAnalyst), QC RSD/detection filtering, deterministic impute->normalize->transform, PCA and original numpy NIPALS PLS-DA with VIP and seeded permutation Q2, Welch/Wilcoxon/Kruskal-Wallis + BH FDR + volcano, deterministic m/z relationship annotation (isotopes/adducts/neutral losses, union-find pseudospectra, MSI level 3), MSP/MGF cosine spectral matching (MSI level 2), and pathway enrichment without built-in databases (ID hypergeometric or mummichog-style m/z permutation against user-supplied licensed mappings). Upstream peak picking has no wrapper here and is reported as a gap; OPLS-DA, drift correction, GSimp, CAMERA full, SIRIUS/MetFrag/GNPS, GC-MS RI, NMR and targeted MRM are documented gaps. Knowledge layer distilled from the RforMassSpectrometry Metabolomics Book (CC-BY-4.0; ideas and structure only, no text or code copied) plus idea-level classical citations (xcms, CAMERA, mummichog, Schymanski MSI levels, PQN, MetaboAnalyst, MassBank/GNPS); the two user-requested Zhihu tutorials were inaccessible (HTTP 403) and are recorded as such. All scripts and prose are original; every produced file carries a contract-1.0.0 artifact descriptor. v0.1.0 is script chain plus knowledge only, no notebook renderer.

Authored in phi-packages. Single-cell ATAC plugin (toolPrefix scatac, agent SingleCellAtac) with one Python-route skill (scatac-workflow, ten scatac_* tools: inspect/qc/preprocess/peaks/markers/annotate/motif/integrate/notebook/env_probe) and one private locked environment plugin:scatac (Python 3.12 + snapatac2 2.10 + scanpy 1.12 + ipykernel, pure conda, three-platform explicit locks solved against the tuna mirror and rewritten to official conda.anaconda.org URLs; macs3 3.1.0 ships as a snapatac2 dependency, no pip). Starts from 10x Cell Ranger ATAC fragments.tsv.gz (or BAM via make_fragment_file, a saved .h5ad, or a peak/tile matrix). assets/fragments (16 steps, 48 parameters, 6 presets) is the single analysis source shared by thin flag-to-config script adapters and the language-neutral notebook renderer (RENDERER_VERSION=3): QC/TSSe, scrublet doublet removal, spectral embedding, kNN/Leiden/UMAP, per-cluster MACS3 peaks + merged peak set + peak-count matrix, marker_regions (cluster-vs-rest) with opt-in pairwise diff_test, gene-activity annotation (panel scoring / scRNA-reference kNN label transfer / explicit mapping), motif enrichment on marker regions, and harmony/scanorama/mnc integration. chrom_sizes bundled offline hg38/mm10/hg19/mm39; ENCODE hg38/mm10 blacklist inlined base64-gzip in assets/fragments/blacklist.py; gene annotation (GFF3 ~50MB) and genome FASTA (~845MB) are snapatac2 lazy downloads supplied by user input-path or reported as gaps, never installed/downloaded into the read-only environment. The TF layer is motif enrichment (sequence-level prediction), not chromVAR per-cell deviations; gene activity is an accessibility proxy, not measured RNA. Raw-read alignment/Cell Ranger ATAC stay on nf-core wrappers; bulk ChIP/CUT&Tag belong to the planned sibling chromatin-profiling plugin. chromVAR/ArchR/Signac (R route), episcanpy (numpy 2 incompatible), scvi-tools/magic-impute (pip-only) and a TF-gene GRN are env_probe project-environment gaps. Knowledge layer: analysis-playbook.md (call/read/decide/red-lines), red-line-cheatsheet.md, 16 step-notes, references README and maintainers/implementation-notes.md, originally distilled from the SnapATAC2 documentation (MIT) and sc-best-practices (Apache 2.0; Heumos, Schaar, Lance et al., Nat Rev Genet 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41576-023-00586-w); ENCODE blacklist doi:10.1038/s41598-019-45839-z. All scripts and prose are original; no upstream text, images or data are copied. v0.1.0.

Authored in phi-packages. Chromatin profiling plugin (toolPrefix chip, agent ChromatinProfiling) with one R-route skill (chromatin-workflow, nine chip_* tools: inspect/qc/consensus/count/diff/annotate/visualize/notebook/env_probe) and one private locked environment plugin:chip (R 4.5 + DiffBind 3.20 + DESeq2 + edgeR + csaw 1.44 + ChIPseeker 1.46 + GenomicAlignments + Rsamtools + GenomicFeatures + ComplexHeatmap + jsonlite, three-platform explicit locks; csaw platform-gated off darwin-arm64 because bioconda has no osx-arm64 build). Bulk ChIP-seq / CUT&Tag / CUT&RUN, PURE DOWNSTREAM: starts from already-called peaks (BED/narrowPeak/broadPeak), a DiffBind sample sheet, a peak x sample count table, indexed BAMs, a bigWig or a saved .rds; never aligns reads or calls peaks (ChIP upstream is the nf-core/chipseq wrapper; CUT&Tag SEACR upstream has no wrapper and is a reported gap). assets/fragments (19 steps) is the single analysis source shared by thin flag-to-config Rscript adapters and the language-neutral notebook renderer (RENDERER_VERSION=3): inspect -> QC (FRiP + replicate peak-overlap reproducibility) -> blacklist filtering -> consensus peakset -> read counting + normalization -> PCA/UpSet -> differential binding (DiffBind/DESeq2/edgeR primary for TF/narrow marks and CUT&Tag; csaw window-based for broad marks) -> ChIPseeker annotation / TSS profiles. Annotation is lean by design: no target-genome TxDb/org.db bundled, ChIPseeker uses makeTxDbFromGFF on the user GTF/GFF3 or loadDb on a user TxDb .sqlite (hg19 never a silent default); gene-symbol org.db mapping is a reported gap. ENCODE v2 hg38 (636 regions) / mm10 (3435 regions) blacklist inlined base64-gzip inside assets/fragments/blacklist-filter.R for offline self-containment (doi:10.1038/s41598-019-45839-z). csaw on darwin-arm64, IDR, profileplyr, HOMER/MEME motif discovery and org.db gene symbols are chip_env_probe project-environment gaps. Knowledge layer: analysis-playbook.md (call/read/decide/red-lines), red-line-cheatsheet.md (12 hard red lines), 19 step-notes, references README and maintainers/implementation-notes.md, originally distilled from the DiffBind / csaw / ChIPseeker vignettes (Artistic-2.0) and ENCODE ChIP-seq guidelines (Landt doi:10.1101/gr.136184.111). All scripts and prose are original; no upstream text, images or data are copied. Single-cell ATAC belongs to the sibling single-cell-atac plugin. v0.1.0.
